_comment: Dinacharya activities (loaded by migrations; edit them in the admin afterwards). start/end: {anchor: sunrise|sunset|clock, offset_minutes, clock, fallback_clock}. {dosha} in text = the user's assessed dosha, {secondary} = their secondary dosha. season_overrides / dosha_overrides replace fields for that season / the user's dominant dosha (dosha wins over season). dosha_tips adds a reason for the dominant dosha and, labelled, for the secondary one. doshas: only include for users whose dominant dosha is listed. above_temperature_c: only include when it is hotter than this. Without a dosha assessment the routine is the general (non-dosha) version.

dosha_focus.vata: Warmth, regularity and grounding: same times every day, warm oiled food, gentle movement, early and steady sleep.
dosha_focus.pitta: Cooling and moderation: avoid overheating and midday sun, favour cool sweet foods, keep exercise non-competitive, wind down before late-night work.
dosha_focus.kapha: Lightness and stimulation: rise early, move vigorously, eat light and warm, and skip the daytime nap.

templates.title: Rise with the day
templates.description: Wake before sunrise; sit quietly for a few minutes.
reasons: Brahma muhurta is associated with a calm mind (classical timing).

vata.description: Wake before sunrise at the same time every day, then sit quietly for a few minutes before getting busy.
reasons: A fixed wake time is one of the most steadying habits for vata, which is easily unsettled by irregularity.

pitta.description: Wake before sunrise and spend a few calm minutes before checking messages or planning the day.
reasons: Starting the day unhurried keeps pitta's sharpness from turning into irritation.

kapha.description: Wake in brahma muhurta and get up straight away; avoid lingering in bed after waking.
reasons: Kapha is heaviest in the early morning; rising early and promptly counters sluggishness.

templates.title: Warm water + tongue cleaning
templates.description: Drink warm water; clean the tongue gently.
reasons: Warm water supports digestion and hydration.

dosha_tips.vata: Sip it warm and slowly; warm liquids counter vata's dryness.
dosha_tips.pitta: Lukewarm rather than hot water suits pitta.
dosha_tips.kapha: Warm water (never iced) helps clear morning heaviness.

templates.title: Self-massage (coconut oil)
templates.description: A short abhyanga with coconut oil before bathing.
reasons: Coconut oil is seasonally balancing for your climate.

shishir.title: Self-massage (sesame oil)
shishir.description: A short abhyanga with sesame oil before bathing.
reasons: Sesame oil is seasonally balancing for your climate.

hemant.title: Self-massage (sesame oil)
hemant.description: A short abhyanga with sesame oil before bathing.
reasons: Sesame oil is seasonally balancing for your climate.

vasant.title: Self-massage (sesame oil)
vasant.description: A short abhyanga with sesame oil before bathing.
reasons: Sesame oil is seasonally balancing for your climate.

vata.title: Daily abhyanga (warm sesame oil)
vata.description: Massage warm sesame oil into the whole body, with extra on the head, ears and soles of the feet. Rest a few minutes, then bathe in warm water.
reasons: Oil massage is the classical counter to vata's dry, rough and cold qualities; vata benefits from it every day.

pitta.title: Abhyanga (coconut oil)
pitta.description: A gentle massage with coconut or sunflower oil at room temperature, then a lukewarm (not hot) bath.
reasons: Cooling oils and lukewarm water keep pitta's heat from building.

kapha.title: Dry massage (udvartana)
kapha.description: Brisk upward strokes with a dry herbal powder or chickpea flour (or a raw-silk glove), then a warm shower. Use oil sparingly, if at all.
reasons: Udvartana (powder massage) reduces kapha and heaviness, where daily oiling would add to it.

templates.title: Breathing practice (pranayama)
templates.description: Ten minutes of slow, even breathing in a quiet place before the day starts.
reasons: Calm breathing settles the mind before activity.

vata.title: Nadi shodhana (alternate-nostril breathing)
vata.description: Ten minutes of slow alternate-nostril breathing, seated comfortably and kept warm.
reasons: Slow, balanced breathing calms vata's restlessness and anxiety.

pitta.title: Sheetali / sheetkari (cooling breath)
pitta.description: Inhale slowly through a curled tongue (or through the teeth) and exhale through the nose, for 5-10 minutes.
reasons: Cooling breaths are traditionally used to release excess pitta heat.

kapha.title: Kapalabhati / bhastrika (energising breath)
kapha.description: A few rounds of brisk, forceful exhalations, resting between rounds. Skip it if you are pregnant or have high blood pressure, heart disease or a hernia.
reasons: Energising breath stimulates kapha's slowness and clears the chest.

templates.title: Movement / exercise
templates.description: Moderate exercise until mild perspiration; stop before exhaustion.
reasons: Exercise supports kapha balance and digestion.

vata.title: Gentle movement (yoga, walking)
vata.description: Slow, grounding practice: gentle yoga, walking or swimming. Stop well before you feel tired.
reasons: Over-exertion aggravates vata; the classical rule is to exercise to only half of one's capacity.

pitta.title: Moderate exercise (in the cool hours)
pitta.description: Swimming, cycling or yoga while it is still cool; avoid competitive, overheated workouts and the midday sun.
reasons: Pitta overheats easily; moderate, non-competitive exercise keeps it balanced.

kapha.title: Vigorous exercise
kapha.description: Your most active session of the day: brisk running, sun salutations or strength work until you sweat.
reasons: Kapha benefits most from vigorous exercise; it clears heaviness and sluggishness.

templates.title: Breakfast (only when hungry)
templates.description: A modest, warm breakfast once the previous evening's meal is digested.
reasons: Eat when the last meal has been digested and hunger has returned.

vata.title: Warm, nourishing breakfast
vata.description: Cooked porridge with a little ghee and stewed fruit. Avoid cold, dry foods such as cereal or raw salads, and don't skip it.
reasons: Warm, moist, regular meals steady vata digestion.

pitta.title: Cooling breakfast
pitta.description: Sweet fruit, oats or rice porridge. Avoid coffee on an empty stomach and spicy, sour or fried food.
reasons: Pitta's strong appetite should be met, with cooling foods, before it turns into irritability.

kapha.title: Light breakfast, or skip it
kapha.description: Only if you are truly hungry: a little warm fruit or a spiced herbal drink. A heavy breakfast slows kapha digestion.
reasons: Kapha digestion is slow in the morning; a light or skipped breakfast is traditionally advised.

templates.title: Main meal
templates.description: Eat your largest meal now, when digestive fire (agni) is strongest. Eat mindfully, until comfortably full.
reasons: Midday is the classical peak of agni.

dosha_tips.vata: Favour warm, moist, well-oiled food with sweet, sour and salty tastes.
dosha_tips.pitta: Favour sweet, bitter and astringent tastes; go easy on chilli, sour and salty food.
dosha_tips.kapha: Favour pungent, bitter and astringent tastes; keep the meal warm, light and low in oil and sweets.

templates.title: Stay out of the harsh sun
templates.description: Keep out of the strongest midday sun; cover your head outdoors and sip cool (not iced) water.
reasons: Midday is pitta time of day; heat and sun push pitta out of balance fastest now.

templates.title: Short walk instead of a nap
templates.description: Stay up after lunch: walk for 10-15 minutes rather than lying down.
reasons: Day sleep increases kapha; the texts allow it mainly in peak summer or for the weak.

templates.title: Warm drink and a pause
templates.description: Late afternoon is vata time of day: stop for a warm drink and a few slow breaths, and have a small snack if you are hungry.
reasons: Vata rises in the late afternoon; warmth and a short pause prevent the usual energy dip and scattered mind.

templates.title: Light dinner
templates.description: Prefer warm, freshly-cooked meals and a 3-hour gap before sleep.
reasons: A light evening meal supports restful sleep.

varsha.description: In the monsoon, digestion is weaker: prefer light, warm, well-spiced food.

grishma.description: In peak summer, favor cool, light meals and hydration.

dosha_tips.vata: A warm soup, khichdi or stew at a regular time; don't skip dinner.
dosha_tips.pitta: A moderate, not spicy meal; avoid alcohol and fermented, sour food in the evening.
dosha_tips.kapha: Make this the lightest meal of the day (soup or steamed vegetables) and finish early.

templates.title: Sunset walk
templates.description: A short evening walk; reduce stimulation as light fades.
reasons: Matching activity to the light cycle steadies the mind.

dosha_tips.vata: Keep it slow and dress warmly; evening wind and cold aggravate vata.
dosha_tips.pitta: An unhurried walk somewhere green or near water is especially cooling.
dosha_tips.kapha: Walk briskly; this is a good second chance to move today.

templates.title: Afternoon rest
templates.description: Very hot weather: rest in a cool, shaded room; hydrate.
reasons: Heat stress is managed by scheduling rest during peak heat.

templates.title: Wind down
templates.description: Dim lights, avoid screens, light reading or quiet reflection.
reasons: Reduced stimulation before sleep improves nidra (restorative sleep).

vata.description: Rub a little warm oil into the soles of the feet, keep lights low and screens off, and go to bed at the same time every night.
reasons: Foot massage (padabhyanga) and a fixed bedtime are classical aids to sleep for vata.

pitta.description: Keep the room cool and quiet; put work, arguments and screens away for the night.
reasons: Late-night work keeps pitta's mind 'switched on'; cooling down first protects sleep.

kapha.description: Light stretching or reading rather than TV on the couch, and nothing more to eat after dinner.
reasons: A little activity and an empty stomach at bedtime keep kapha from feeling heavy next morning.

templates.title: Sleep
reasons: Regular, sufficient sleep is one of the three pillars of health (with food and right conduct).

vata.description: Aim for 7-8 hours at a fixed bedtime. Your routine is tuned to a {dosha} constitution.
reasons: Vata needs the most regular and the most sleep of the three doshas.

kapha.description: Sleep early and rise early: about 7 hours is enough. Your routine is tuned to a {dosha} constitution.
reasons: Kapha-predominant people do best sleeping early and not oversleeping.

pitta.description: Be in bed by 22:30, before the late-night pitta period keeps you working. Your routine is tuned to a {dosha} constitution.
reasons: The late-night hours are pitta time; staying up past them invites a 'second wind' and poor sleep.
